seo.title: AI Mode Temporary Threads: What It Means for You
seo.meta_description: AI Mode temporary threads let people search without saving history or personalization. What that means for how Anaheim and Orange County businesses get found.

h1: AI Mode Temporary Threads: When Searches Aren't Personalized, Clear Business Information Wins
answer: AI Mode temporary threads, introduced November 17, 2026, let people ask AI Mode questions in a session detached from their account, so answers aren't informed by past preferences, don't affect future personalization and aren't saved to history. For Anaheim and Orange County businesses, it means some AI Mode answers rely only on public information, so a clear website, Business Profile and reviews matter even more.
key_takeaways: Sessions are detached from the user's account.
Answers aren't informed by past preferences.
Nothing is saved to history once the thread closes.
Public business information carries the answer.

sections.heading: What Google announced
sections.body_html: On November 17, 2026, Google introduced temporary threads in AI Mode. People can explore and ask questions, such as brainstorming a surprise gift, without the conversation resurfacing later in their history or recommendations.

sections.heading: How temporary threads work
sections.body_html: Google says people click the temporary threads icon in the upper right of AI Mode. Because the session is completely detached from the account, responses aren't informed by past preferences, don't affect future personalization and aren't saved to history. When the thread closes, it's gone.

sections.heading: Where it's available
sections.body_html: Google says the feature is rolling out globally on desktop and mobile browsers in all languages supported in AI Mode.

sections.heading: Why this matters for businesses
sections.body_html: In a temporary thread, AI Mode can't lean on what it knows about the person's past preferences or saved places. Its answer depends on public information about businesses: websites, Business Profiles, reviews and other sources it can find.

sections.heading: Gift shopping is a key use
sections.body_html: Google's own example is brainstorming a surprise gift. For retailers in Orange County, that means gift searches in temporary threads may rely more on clear product information, availability and reviews than on a shopper's history.

sections.heading: What makes public information strong
sections.body_html:
• A website that says plainly what you sell or do, for whom and where.
  • A complete Google Business Profile with accurate hours and services.
  • Genuine reviews that describe real purchases or jobs.
  • Consistent details across directories and maps.
  • Product data on Google for retailers.

sections.heading: Personalization isn't a strategy
sections.body_html: Some businesses rely on repeat customers seeing them because they visited before. Temporary threads are a reminder that plenty of searches don't carry that history, so a business must be easy to understand for someone who has never heard of it.

sections.heading: What to check this week
sections.body_html:
1. Read your homepage as a stranger would.
  2. Make sure each service or product category has its own clear page.
  3. Check your Business Profile is complete.
  4. Ask recent customers for reviews.
  5. For retailers, check product data on Google.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body_html: Imagine a gift boutique in Tustin. A shopper uses a temporary thread to brainstorm a gift for a coworker who loves cooking, so AI Mode has no history to draw on. Because the boutique's website lists its kitchen gifts with clear descriptions, its Business Profile is complete and recent reviews mention thoughtful gifts, it is a reasonable shop for AI Mode to suggest.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether temporary threads hurt their visibility. They don't target businesses; they remove personal history from the answer, which makes public information more important. Another common question is whether businesses can see who searched in a temporary thread. No; the session isn't tied to the person's account. Owners also ask whether this changes SEO basics. No; it reinforces them.

sections.heading: Gift and surprise purchases
sections.body_html: Searches people want to keep private, such as gifts or surprises, are exactly where temporary threads are likely to be used. Gift shops, florists, jewelers and experience businesses should make gift ideas, price ranges and delivery or pickup options easy to find.

sections.heading: Answer common questions directly
sections.body_html: AI answers draw on pages that answer questions clearly. A short FAQ on each service or product page, answering what people ask before buying, gives AI Mode concise, accurate material to work with.

sections.heading: Keep details consistent
sections.body_html: When answers rely on public information alone, conflicting details, such as different hours on your website and Business Profile, are more likely to cause confusion. Check that your name, address, phone, hours and services match everywhere.

sections.heading: Reviews describe you to strangers
sections.body_html: For someone with no history with your business, reviews are often the most persuasive information. Ask for reviews steadily, and reply to them, so recent experiences describe your business accurately.

sections.heading: Measure what you can
sections.body_html: Search Console's generative AI performance report shows how often your pages appear in AI features. Watch it alongside calls and visits to see whether clearer pages lead to more visibility.

sections.heading: Think like a first-time customer
sections.body_html: A useful exercise is to ask a friend who doesn't know your business to describe what you do after a minute on your website. If they can't, neither can an AI system relying only on public information.

sections.heading: Writing pages a stranger understands
sections.body_html: Imagine a customer who has never heard of you, asking an AI assistant for a recommendation with no history to draw on. What would it need to know to suggest you? Start each important page with one or two sentences that say what you do, for whom and where, such as family dentistry in Tustin with Saturday hours. Follow with the details people compare: services, price ranges or how pricing works, availability and what makes you different. Avoid vague slogans, which give an AI system nothing concrete to use.

sections.heading: Structured data helps machines read you
sections.body_html: Structured data, such as LocalBusiness or Product markup, states key facts in a format search systems can read reliably: your name, address, phone, hours, products and prices. It doesn't guarantee anything, but it reduces ambiguity, which matters more when answers rely only on public information. Make sure the details in your markup match what's visible on the page and on your Business Profile.

sections.heading: Reviews that help strangers decide
sections.body_html: When someone has no history with your business, reviews describing real experiences carry extra weight. Encourage customers to mention what they bought or what you did for them, and how it went. Reply to reviews in a helpful, specific way. Over time, these reviews give AI systems and people alike a clear, trustworthy picture of your business, even in a temporary thread.

sections.heading: Local details make a difference
sections.body_html: For a local business, the details a stranger needs usually include where you are, which areas you serve, when you're open and how to get in touch or book. Put these on every important page, not only the contact page, and keep them identical to your Business Profile. For businesses in Anaheim and across Orange County, naming the city and neighborhood naturally in your page text helps search systems connect you to local questions, whether or not the person asking has any history with you.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: AI Mode temporary threads give answers without personal history, relying on public information. Anaheim and Orange County businesses should make their websites, Business Profiles, reviews and product data clear and consistent, so they're easy to recommend to anyone.

faqs.q: What are AI Mode temporary threads?
faqs.a: Sessions in AI Mode detached from the user's account, not saved to history or used for personalization.
Google says globally on desktop and mobile browsers in AI Mode's supported languages.
No; they make public business information more important.

faqs.q: Can businesses see temporary thread searches?
faqs.a: No. Sessions aren't tied to the person's account.
Keep websites, Business Profiles, reviews and product data clear and consistent.
